    Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has won the 2026 American League MVP, the BBWAA unveiled Thursday night.

    Industry observers note that the Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing AL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

    Alvarez, 29, bounced back from an injury-riddled disaster in 2025, during which he only played in 48 games. This time around, he avoided the IL and appeared in 158 games. He hit .316/.432/.601 (190 OPS+) with 34 doubles, a triple, 42 home runs, 106 RBI, 105 runs and 6.8 WAR. He made a late run at the Triple Crown, missing out by one home run and seven RBI. He did lead the majors in all three triple slash categories, though, leading in average by five points, on-base percentage by a whopping 42 points -- he led the majors in walks -- and 31 points in slugging percentage. Add the latter two and his OPS victory was 90 points -- 1.033 to second place's .943 (National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong).

    The only players in MLB history to lead the majors in all three triple slash categories:.

    Alvarez becomes just the third Astros player to win MVP after Jeff Bagwell in 1994 and Jose Altuve in 2017.

    Industry observers note that rays third baseman Junior Caminero finished in second. At age 22, he played all 162 games, leading the Rays to the best AL record. He hit .276/.360/.524 (144 OPS+) with 42 home runs, 101 RBI and 100 runs, posting a 5.7 WAR. He's already made history, too, as the Rays had previously never had a player finish in the top five of MVP voting.

    Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. came in third. This is now his fourth straight season in the top seven and third straight season in the top four. He finished second in 2024. This season, he hit .281/.359/.441 (125 OPS+) with 33 doubles, 18 homers, 54 RBI, 94 runs, 45 steals and 6.7 WAR.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Things got heated between the Rockets and Warriors on Wednesday, with Marcus Smart getting ejected late in the third quarter for throwing a punch at the head area of Golden State's Charles Bassey.

    Smart and Bassey had gotten tangled up on the other end. After they disconnected and Bassey made his way back on defense, Smart chased after Bassey from behind, made contact, swung around to his front side, and threw the blow that is likely going to lead to a suspension.

    MARCUS SMART PUNCHES CHARLES BASSEY 😳 pic.twitter.com/MUsLlDHCz4.

    What did Bassey do, or say, that got Smart so riled up?

    It has been revealed that "I just talked to [Smart]. He noted they got wrapped up, and [Smart]'s elbow that he hurt got bent up," Rockets coach Ime Udoka explained after the game. "So, [Smart] said something to him. Bassey said, 'What are you going to do?' And he did it.".

    You can see a better view of the play here.

    Looks Like Charles Bassey Had His Arm Tangled Up With Marcus Smart Before The Punch.Nothing Too Serious, Why Did He React Like That? https://t.co/d96UmqUDpM pic.twitter.com/5tmUbokqHR.

    Recent findings suggest that smart was hit with a flagrant-2 foul, which carries an automatic ejection (the 13th of Smart's career). Smart didn't stick around long after he threw the punch. As players were being separated to keep things from escalating any further, Smart almost immediately took off his elbow sleeve and walked straight to the locker room. He knew he was gone.

    As for Bassey's side of the story, the Warriors' big man stated Smart was "playing dirty" all night.

    "He's been playing dirty the whole game," Bassey said. "In the first half, I was trying to set a screen and he grabbed my knee. So I mean, he was playing dirty. [On the play in question], I think I was trying to get a rebound and he was grabbing my hand and I was trying to run back on defense. ... And then he got up on me and swung. Obviously that was weak. I think that was, honestly, fake toughness.".

    It has been revealed that asked whether he said anything to Smart to set him off, Bassey explained: "He said something to me. He said something like, 'Hey, don't do that.' I said, 'Do what?' It's a grown-man's league.".

    Charles Bassey calls out Marcus Smart for being a fake tough guy and a dirty player 😬(Via @anthonyVslater ) pic.twitter.com/l461taMhtS.

    As for how long Smart will be out, here's the league's wording on punches thrown from the NBA's official rule book.

    So Smart is out at least one game and, again, almost certainly a good chunk of cash.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the National League MVP award for the 2026 season unanimously, the BBWAA revealed Thursday evening.

    The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing NL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

    Though the results were unsurprising by the time the year wound down, going back to the start of the season, this marks a huge upset. Shohei Ohtani was the overwhelming favorite to win the award heading into the season and maintained favorite status through the All-Star break. A combination of his injuries and PCA's monster season turned the tide late.

    According to recent reports, appearing in all 162 games, Crow-Armstrong hit .280/.372/.570 (156 OPS+) with 31 doubles, eight triples, 45 home runs, 107 RBI, 119 runs, 41 steals and 9.8 WAR. He led the majors in WAR, runs, home runs and total bases while leading the NL in slugging, OPS and OPS+. He became the seventh player in MLB history to join the 40-40 club (40 home runs and 40 steals in the same season). Further, he led the majors in multiple advanced defensive metrics, putting together one of the great all-around seasons from a position player in recent memory.

    PCA joins the following list of Cubs to win MVP:.

    Sources indicate that ohtani, the four-time MVP, finishes in second. At the plate, Ohtani hit .275/.377/.512 with 26 doubles, four triples, 30 home runs, 81 RBI, 89 runs, 11 steals and 3.2 WAR. On the mound, he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 95 strikeouts in 85 ⅔ innings with 3.2 WAR.

    According to recent reports, the nationally underrated Brewers second baseman Brice Turang finishes in third. He still hasn't made an All-Star Game, though he did start 2026 as a member of Team USA in the World Baseball Classic. In the regular season, Turang hit .268/.366/.450 (124 OPS+) with 37 doubles, three triples, 21 home runs, 100 RBI, 102 runs and 7.3 WAR, rating out as one of the best defenders in baseball.

    • Two days after losing by 51 points to the Golden State Warriors, the Newly introduced Orleans Pelicans managed an even more embarrassing loss on Wednesday when they were blown out 145-111 by the Brooklyn Nets, who were 2-8 entering the night.
    • Latest Orleans (4-8) began the season on a four-game losing streak before bouncing back to .500 with a four-game winning streak, but has now lost four straight again.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Two days after losing by 51 points to the Golden State Warriors, the Newly introduced Orleans Pelicans managed an even more embarrassing loss on Wednesday when they were blown out 145-111 by the Brooklyn Nets, who were 2-8 entering the night.

    Latest Orleans (4-8) began the season on a four-game losing streak before bouncing back to .500 with a four-game winning streak, but has now lost four straight again. The concerning part of their recent skid is that the Pelicans have grown increasingly uncompetitive.

    According to recent reports, in that initial four-game losing streak to open the season, the Pelicans lost by a combined 23 points in the four games. In their last two games, they've lost by a combined 85 points, leaving Zion Williamson with just one word to describe his team's effort.

    "Unacceptable," Williamson stated, via ESPN. "I don't even have a lot of words. Just unacceptable.".

    It has been revealed that williamson called out the Pelicans' defensive effort during this latest losing streak, as they've allowed at least 138 points in three consecutive games. The seventh-year star then called for his team to look inward and be honest with themselves about whether they're doing everything they can to help the team win.

    Recent findings suggest that "I stated nobody likes to lose like this, but if we don't like to lose like this, we have to start with ourselves first," Williamson said. "Look in the mirror and say, did I do what I needed to do for my team? Not individually. Did I do what I needed to do for my team? And then we go from there.".

    It's never a good sign when a team's star is questioning the collective's effort level and commitment to winning just 12 games into the season. This is when buy-in should be the easiest to get because a team's goals are still right in front of them, but the Pelicans are already showing signs that they will likely spend another season at the bottom of the Western Conference.

    It has been revealed that that four-game winning streak -- which was somewhat schedule-aided with two games against the woeful Sacramento Kings and Utah Jazz -- feels like ages ago for the Pelicans. If they're going to turn things around, Williamson is right that it starts with accountability from the players, but with some key injuries to Trey Murphy III and Yves Missi, coupled with poor play, this season could get away from New Orleans swiftly.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that week 10 in the NFL offers the first look at most teams in the wake of the Nov.
    • Other deals have not aged nearly as well.
    • Sources indicate that not all of this week's top takeaways revolve around trade deadline fallout, though.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that week 10 in the NFL offers the first look at most teams in the wake of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Early returns are in on the majority of the 17 in-season transactions. A couple of newcomers have yet to debut with their latest squads, but there is already a clear frontrunner for the most impactful trade of the year after Kirk Cousins' first game with the Minnesota Vikings.

    Other deals have not aged nearly as well. For instance, Marvin Harrison Jr. was inactive for the Houston Texans on Sunday, was not all that productive in his first three games with the franchise and watched his teammates take a bad loss when they threw away a 17-point lead to the Cleveland Browns.

    Sources indicate that not all of this week's top takeaways revolve around trade deadline fallout, though. Division races and injuries are, as always, a large part of the picture.

    Here are the biggest winners and losers from Sunday's NFL Week 10 action.

    As winners of three of four games heading into Week 10, and with a 17-0 first-half lead over the Browns, the Houston Texans were in an ideal position to climb back into the playoff race after a 0-4 start to the season. Surely, with C.J. Stroud playing the best football of his career and Will Anderson Jr. pinning his ears back against the trailing Browns, that three-possession lead had to be safe, right? Not so fast.

    The Texans and a defense that has been a disappointment all year surrendered 20 unanswered points in the second and third quarters. The lead evaporated. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson threw for 312 yards and a touchdown and tacked on another 49 yards and a score on the ground. He orchestrated yet another comeback—the Browns have trailed or been tied in every fourth quarter this season—and helped Cleveland improve to 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963. Watson did all that against what was supposed to be the NFL's best defense.

    That unit's inability to carry its 2025 dominance into 2026 has been the primary factor behind Houston's underwhelming season. Nothing the Texans have done to address it has worked, including a change of play-caller. Each of their last four opponents scored at least 21 points.

    In turn, Houston is three games back of .500 at 3-6 and has practically no margin for error remaining in its hunt for a postseason berth. That is why only one team in NFL history has ever started a year at 0-4 and still made the playoffs. The climb out of the hole is steep, and the reasons behind a poor start are usually season-defining. They certainly are for the Texans.

    The Vikings were so universally celebrated at the trade deadline because if Cousins could deliver even a modicum of improvement to an anemic offense, the team's ceiling would skyrocket. One game into his reunion with the franchise, he already delivered exactly what was envisioned. Minnesota's top-ranked defense did its thing in a 30-10 beatdown of the Green Bay Packers, and instead of just skating by on the other side of the ball, the Vikings finally pulled away from an opponent.

    Cousins went 21-for-31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. He freed Justin Jefferson from his season-long frustration, finding the superstar wide receiver nine times for 74 yards. As a result, the Vikings turned in their second 30-point outing of the campaign and the first since they exploded against that same Packers team in the season opener.

    In a recent development, minnesota's trade deadline transaction helped snap a two-game losing skid. It also solidified a head-to-head tiebreaker over the Packers in the NFL's most competitive division. The Cousins deal is already a home-run trade.

    Recent findings suggest that other familiar faces in latest places this week included Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Josh Downs and Buffalo Bills safety Amani Hooker. They also did their front offices proud in blowout wins. Downs hauled in his longest touchdown since 2024 to help the Chiefs score 35 points for the second consecutive week, while Hooker racked up seven tackles to rank third on the Bills defense.

    Sources indicate that it was the same old song and dance with the Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 10. The maligned unit wasted a tremendous offensive performance that included five passing touchdowns from Dak Prescott, three of which went to George Pickens, in a 46-40 loss to the NFC's best team: the San Francisco 49ers. The 584 yards they allowed were the most in a home game in franchise history, and the 46 points were the fourth most.

    Explosive plays were easy to come by for the 49ers in a game that set series records for combined points and yards. Christian McCaffrey recorded the longest receiving touchdown of his career with a 74-yarder and followed it up with a 66-yard catch-and-run later in the game. Deebo Samuel broke loose for a 70-yard run on a reverse that completely confused Dallas' defense.

    DEEEEEEBOOOOOOOSFvsDAL on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3RwQ4dNchJ.

    For context on McCaffrey, a few notes from CBS Sports research and ESPN Insights:.

    The Cowboys had a tremendous opportunity to capitalize on the Upcoming York Giants' loss and move closer to the NFC East lead. Their defense blew it.

    The same week most of the NFL's top trade deadline movers debuted with their new teams, Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III watched theirs win without them. The former Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle and ex-Falcons safety hadn't hit their bye weeks yet when the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for them, so coach Liam Coen gave them the week off to rest while they acclimated to their new surroundings.

    Recent findings suggest that the Jaguars did not need them anyway. They rolled to a 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans. They would have been better off with both newcomers in the lineup, since they are standouts at positions that have thinned out in Jacksonville in recent weeks, and the squad gave up its second-highest point total of the year without them. But it should be a promising sign that the Super Bowl contenders can cruise past a bottom-dwelling opponent with a couple of glaring holes on their defense. Just imagine what Jacksonville will do to Tennessee at home in two weeks when Davis and Bates are active.

    There might not be a more unfortunate way to sustain a serious injury in the course of an NFL game than while celebrating. Detroit Lions star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson experienced that harsh reality firsthand in Munich. He went down with a non-contact knee injury in the Week 10 international game after landing awkwardly while celebrating a sack on New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.

    Aidan Hutchinson just got hurt celebrating a sack pic.twitter.com/bz1CY4G4Av.

    Recent findings suggest that the Lions reportedly fear that Hutchinson sustained a significant injury that will sideline him for the foreseeable future. He and the team are seeking second opinions following the initial tests in Germany, but early indications suggest his season may be over.

    Beyond the unfortunate freakiness of how the injury occurred, this is also a devastating blow to a Lions defense that seems to be turning a corner for the better. What has all season been a bottom-tier unit in limiting opposing teams' yardage has not allowed more than two touchdowns in a game since Oct. 11. It will be hard-pressed to keep that streak going much longer without its most disruptive player.

    In a recent development, patrick Mahomes was already the leading candidate for Comeback Player of the Year and boosted his chances even higher with his best game of the season. In a 35-13 demolition of the Atlanta Falcons, Mahomes passed for 348 yards and five touchdowns and set a latest NFL record for passing touchdowns (328) by a player in his first 10 seasons. He passed Peyton Manning on that leaderboard.

    The most impressive part of Mahomes' monster performance was that he and the Kansas City Chiefs torched Atlanta's defense even without star running back Kenneth Walker III in the lineup. Instead, rookie Emmett Johnson picked up the slack on the ground and turned into Mahomes' favorite option in the passing game. They linked up six times for 70 yards and a pair of touchdowns through the air.

    According to recent reports, congratulations are in order for Fernando Mendoza on making the first start of many in what could be a glorious professional career. Outside of scoring his first touchdown on a 10-yard run, however, there were not too many bright spots in the No. 1 draft pick's starting debut. He fared decently well on an individual level, particularly considering he matched up against a deadly Seattle Seahawks defense, but the rest of his supporting cast and the Las Vegas Raiders' defense did not hold up their ends of the bargain in a 21-13 loss.

    Fernando Mendoza rushes it in for his first career TD 🗣️SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gcKUNMIZUH.

    The offensive line failed Mendoza and routinely left oncoming pass rushers unblocked en route to allowing six sacks. Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. combined to average a paltry 2.4 yards per carry. Brock Bowers left with an ankle injury, and the wide receivers were non-impactful in his absence. The defense put pressure on him in the second half when it surrendered a pair of touchdowns and tasked him with outdueling Drew Lock and Jaxon Smith-Njigba -- the former of whom completed 14 of 17 passes and the latter of whom racked up 171 receiving yards.

    Better days will surely be ahead for Mendoza, but Sunday was a reminder that the Raiders are still a rebuilding team and far from a perfect situation for a young quarterback.

    The Los Angeles Rams had plenty of reasons not to steamroll the Arizona Cardinals with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams headlining a laundry list of injuries and with the Cardinals pulling off an upset in their first meeting. They rolled to a 34-6 blowout win on the road regardless, and they did so with meaningful contributions from playmakers across the board. It was perhaps the first real showing of how this team's depth can carry them to tremendous heights.

    Sources indicate that byron Young, Braden Fiske, Tyler Davis and Shaun Dolac teed off on rookie quarterback Carson Beck with a sack apiece. Aaron Donald led the charge in the pass rush with 1.5 sacks and brought down the quarterback for the first time since he came out of retirement earlier this season. On the back end, Kamren Kinchens and Wesley Bailey hauled in an interception each. Offensively, Matthew Stafford passed for three touchdowns and Blake Corum logged the second 100-yard game of his career as the leader of the rushing attack.

    Context matters quite a bit in that the Cardinals started a rookie who was previously their third-string quarterback and that their wide receiver group is a shell of its former self. But what more is there to ask of the Rams in this kind of spot? Job done.

    The Patriots just cannot get healthy. A whopping 42 players have started for them this season, which is nearly an average of two per position. That number will grow next week if Drake Maye misses time due to the ankle injury he sustained in the Munich Game. The third-year quarterback lasted all of one drive before leaving for the locker room after the same play in which Hutchinson sustained his knee concern. Tommy DeVito entered in relief of Maye and did little as the leader of the offense, completing just 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. The Patriots scored once without Maye on the field.

    The number of key players to sustain injuries on Monday made an already concerning situation worse in New England.

    Brown made a 22-yard catch just before his day was cut short. He finished the contest with two receptions. His season has been a complete disaster due to a high ankle sprain, his knee condition, and Sunday's hamstring issue. The trade in which the Patriots gave up a first-round pick to acquire him continues to age poorly.

    Recent findings suggest that someone has to win the NFC South, even if they post a losing record in doing so. The Carolina Panthers did just that in 2025 and are on track to do it again for a second straight year. They are the first team in the division to reach four wins, thanks to their 20-17 win over the Newly introduced Orleans Saints, which came on a 54-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald as time expired.

    The game-winning kick concluded a three-game losing streak. Without Chuba Hubbard, the Panthers would not have been in a position to win on the game's final play. The standout running back gained 172 yards from scrimmage as the team's top rusher and receiver on the day and ran for two touchdowns.

    Onside kick recoveries are practically a thing of the past, but the Falcons pulled one in during their loss to the Chiefs. It had no impact on the game's outcome but was notable because of what it meant in the league context. It was the first successful onside kick in the NFL this season, with 23 attempts, and thus ended the longest streak without a recovery to start a season since 2000.

    Industry observers note that you won’t see an onside kick prettier than this. pic.twitter.com/1oSTxR1Hq0.

    It has been revealed that from that 2000 season through 2017, onside kicks were successful 19.5% of the time. From the following year -- when the NFL banned running starts – to the implementation of the dynamic kickoff in 2024, the success rate dipped all the way down to 8.7%. Even though the league walked back some of its restrictions, the remaining rules and the inability to pull off surprise onside kicks kept the recovery percentage extremely low.

    Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

    Industry observers note that alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

    Industry observers note that but perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

    “The data is not key,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”.

    Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

    Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

    Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

    Sources indicate that “After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso stated. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”.

    According to recent reports, it is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

    Recent findings suggest that alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

    After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

    "It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0.

    But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

    Recent findings suggest that neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

    “I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”.

    According to recent reports, conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

    Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was rapidly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

    Sources indicate that “We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso remarked. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”.

    Chelsea’s upcoming set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

    Recent findings suggest that macPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”.

    Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

    Recent findings suggest that xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

    Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

    According to recent reports, “It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso remarked. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”.

    It has been revealed that brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

    According to recent reports, “When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

    “We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very crucial to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”.

    Sources indicate that brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

    • Sources indicate that the injury happened halfway through the first quarter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Golden State Warriors' fairytale start to the season got a dose of reality on Wednesday when Stephen Curry suffered an injury to his oblique in a loss to the Houston Rockets.

    Sources indicate that an MRI on Thursday confirmed an oblique abdominal tear and the team unveiled that Curry will be re-evaluated in two weeks. While two weeks is the best-case scenario, that being just the re-evaluation point means his absence could extend beyond that timetable -- as that also doesn't include any ramp-up process he would need to clear before returning to the floor.

    Sources indicate that the injury happened halfway through the first quarter. You can see Curry get tangled up with Alperen Sengun and grab at his side after they separate.

    Steph Curry got injured after Sengun grabbed and twisted his arm pic.twitter.com/4p20Rogpeu.

    Moments later, Curry hit his lone 3-pointer of the game and could once again be seen grabbing at his side after the shot.

    Stephen Curry headed to the locker room with an apparent right hip injury. pic.twitter.com/1zVrNz00bH.

    It has been revealed that curry exited the game at the next dead ball and didn't return. After the game, Warriors coach Steve Kerr mentioned concern about Curry's injury was "high.".

    "He mentioned he tweaked something in his abdominal area," Kerr said. "He said he's never done it before. ... Concern is high, but I have no idea the extent of the injury.".

    In recent seasons, the range of recovery times for other notable NBA oblique injuries has varied.

    Industry observers note that it's unclear how severe Curry's oblique tear is. These are all strains, which is code for a minor tear, but the worst-case scenario would be a more severe one. We saw this two years ago when the Orlando Magic lost both Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero to oblique tears that kept Banchero out for 10 weeks and Wagner for more than a month.

    Any extended absence would be disastrous for the Warriors, who are not equipped to cover for any Curry injury. Curry has gotten off to a scorching start, entering Wednesday averaging 30.1 points per game on 50.3/45.7/98.7 shooting splits with Golden State winning eight straight games for the first time since the 2022 championship season.

    Industry observers note that but this was always a fingers-crossed situation with an aging roster. Already down Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porziņģis, and with Brandon Williams and Gary Payton II also on the shelf and wing Will Richard playing through a ligament tear in his thumb, the Warriors have little, if any, margin for any more injuries.

    It has been revealed that this comes at a particularly tough time for the Warriors, who are entering their most difficult stretch of the season. On Friday, they'll visit the San Antonio Spurs before facing the Dallas Mavericks and Latest Orleans Pelicans on a back-to-back.

    The Warriors have opened up at 8-4 with a top-three offense, but that can go south very rapidly without Curry.

    Curry is the latest NBA star to face an extended injury absence in the first month of the 2026-27 season. Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren (Thunder), Anthony Edwards (Timberwolves), Tyrese Haliburton (Pacers), Kawhi Leonard (Raptors), Paolo Banchero (Magic), Jalen Duren (Pistons) and Kon Knueppel (Hornets) are among the players currently dealing with multi-week absences.

    #3190. Now with an MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong is on the path for an all-time great career. Where could he stack up?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1128 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Now with an MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong is on the path for an all-time great career. Where could he stack up?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1128 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.
    • Industry observers note that crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors.
    • According to recent reports, so what's next?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.

    Industry observers note that crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors. He hit .280/.372/.570 with stellar defense, led the league in home runs (tied with Kyle Schwarber) and massively upgraded his on-base skills. Now, just a few months shy of his 25th birthday, he has an MVP to his name.

    According to recent reports, so what's next? To answer that, we'll look backwards.

    Since integration, only eight center fielders have posted at least 8.0 WAR in a season age-25 or younger: Willie Mays, Mickey Mantle, Willie Davis, César Cedeño, Ken Griffey Jr., Andruw Jones, Mike Trout and PCA. The only ones to top PCA's 9.8 were Mays, Mantle and Trout. If we went back to pre-integration, Tris Speaker and Ty Cobb were the only others who bested PCA here.

    What road map will PCA's career follow?

    Willie Davis was an inconsistent hitter through his age-23 season but had flashed a nice power-speed combo. Sound familiar? That gaudy 8.4 WAR total in 1964, though, was driven largely by monster defensive metrics. Davis hit .294/.316/.413 (110 OPS+) with 23 doubles, seven triples, 12 home runs, 77 RBI, 91 runs and 42 steals. There's little doubt that PCA's 2026 season dwarfed this one overall, and Davis was far behind Mays (11.0) for the league lead in WAR.

    For the rest of his career, Davis averaged 3.1 WAR per season, and though he had good years, he never reached 6.0 WAR again. The WAR figure was, again, mostly driven by defense. He had several good offensive seasons, but his only 20-homer season came in 1962 when he was 22, two years prior to his career year.

    Recent findings suggest that davis' career probably looks a lot like PCA's apparent upside before his home run barrage in the first half of 2025. He racked up over 60 career WAR with a decent batting average, excellent defense and excellent baserunning.

    With PCA reaching 30-30 last year and 40-40 this year, though, the bar has been raised.

    Recent findings suggest that césar Cedeño followed up his 8.0 WAR season with a 7.4 season at age 22 and 5.8 at age 23. He was very good through age 29 and, in fact, the most statistically similar player through both ages 27 and 28 was Hall of Famer Carl Yastrzemski. Things fell apart after that. As a quick and easy way to illustrate it, Cedeño amassed 49.4 WAR through his age-29 season and only 3.6 in his final six years.

    Sources indicate that it's easier to remember that Andruw Jones' career unfolded in similar fashion because we witnessed it not too long ago and then discussed his Hall of Fame candidacy during his nine turns on the ballot before he finally made it in. In Jones' 12 Braves' season, he racked up 368 home runs, 1,117 RBI and 61 WAR while generally being considered the best defensive center fielder in baseball. Once he left, in time for his age-31 season, Jones accrued just 1.7 WAR in his last five seasons.

    Through Jones' age-28 season, the most statistically similar players are Bryce Harper and Frank Robinson.

    To compare these two to Crow-Armstrong, the argument would be that he'll continue to look like one of the best players in baseball -- even if taking steps backward from being the very best in the 2026 regular season -- before falling apart once he's around 30 years old.

    Industry observers note that certainly possible, but given the adjustments he's already not only been willing to make at the plate, but eager to make, I'm just not seeing him all of a sudden hitting a wall. Sure, at some point he'll start losing speed and that'll affect his defensive range and baserunning, but why would the plate skills deteriorate all of a sudden?

    Then again, few saw it coming with Jones.

    All three of these players were on the path to having an argument as the best player in history before injuries derailed them in their 30s and left them as mere "all-time greats.".

    Sources indicate that through Mickey Mantle's age-30 season, he had 90.7 WAR. He averaged 121 games per year in his final six seasons, putting up 19.5 WAR. Through  Ken Griffey Jr.'s age-30 season, he had 76.2 WAR. He played 10 more seasons, but only amassed 7.6 more WAR. Through Mike Trout's age-27 season, he had 72.1 WAR (his top statistical similars were Mantle, Robinson and Griffey). We'll skip 2020 for obvious reasons, but since then he's averaged 90 games and 3.0 WAR per season.

    According to recent reports, even with the drop-offs, it would be surprising to see Crow-Armstrong reach this level because it's surprising to see any player reach this lofty standard. In career WAR among center fielders, Mantle is fourth, Trout is fifth and Griffey is sixth. They trail only Cobb, Speaker and the guy we're going to discuss next. Joe DiMaggio is seventh.

    Despite the lofty standard PCA set for himself in 2026, coming close to Willie Mays' career would be jaw-droppingly shocking, and that is absolutely not intended as a slight.

    Recent findings suggest that mays has an argument as the greatest player in baseball history and he put himself in that discussion by being good at everything and doing it all with great longevity. From his age-23 to -35 seasons, he led the majors in WAR eight times, leading the NL an additional two times. His worst seasons in that timeframe were 7.6 and 7.8 WAR. In that span, he also led the league in runs twice, hits once, triples three times, home runs three times, stolen bases four times, average once, on-base percentage once, slugging percentage five times and OPS five times.

    In a recent development, mays even posted 5.2 WAR at age 39 and 6.3 at age 40. He led the NL with a .425 OBP when he was 40 years old! He hit .345/.411/.667 at age 23.

    Mays' 156.2 career WAR ranks third among position players all-time behind two guys you might have heard of: Barry Bonds (162.8) and Babe Ruth (162.3).

    I feel pretty strongly Pete Crow-Armstrong isn't headed for a run at this career and that's just fine.

    The realistic long-term range for the 2026 National League MVP seems somewhere between Cedeño and Mantle. It's a wide variance of outcomes between those two, obviously, as well it should be when the player we discuss is only 24 years old. For his name to be mentioned among these at all is a testament to the year Crow-Armstrong just put together.

    Tech Report: 'I feel betrayed, misled, in shock. It was a stupid thing for them to do': ANDY WOODMAN relives the moment he was 'brutally' sacked by Bromley - and how his best mate Sir Gareth Southgate helped him cope

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1464 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 11 November 2026.
    • Every sacked manager has a sob story – but few dismissals have felt as harsh as Bromley’s recent decision to part ways with Andy Woodman.
    • It has been revealed that pound for pound, no club has outperformed their history, budget and expectations in English football across the last decade as much as Bromley.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

    Published: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 11 November 2026.

    Every sacked manager has a sob story – but few dismissals have felt as harsh as Bromley’s recent decision to part ways with Andy Woodman.

    It has been revealed that pound for pound, no club has outperformed their history, budget and expectations in English football across the last decade as much as Bromley. But after an understandably tricky start in League One – two wins from their first 10 games – Woodman was shown the door.

    Sources indicate that in his first interview since that decision last month, the 55-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport about feelings of 'betrayal' and 'shock' before making his pitch to future employers. But the most eye-opening part of our candid conversation comes when I ask the man with more than four decades of experience to recall the club he took over in 2021.

    Industry observers note that ‘Look, Bromley is your classic non-League club,’ says Woodman. ‘I mean that with the greatest respect to all non-League clubs and I hate the word “non-League” as I think it should be “League Three”, as they are all professional.

    Recent findings suggest that ‘But the facilities are non-League, the mentality is non-League. Everything is done day-to-day, hand-to-mouth, every penny counts, every decision that costs money counts, it is run by people’s personal money.

    ‘It was tough when I started: we had no turnstiles, no club shop, we trained on the pitch because it was astroturf, we had no gym.’.

    Andy Woodman was sacked as Bromley boss last month despite leading the club to the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season.

    Woodman with the FA Trophy in 2022. 'Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair,' states the former Bromley boss.

    Under chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves, Woodman and Co, Bromley changed this mentality and shot up the pyramid, winning the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season. Two months later, it was all over.

    Recent findings suggest that asked how he feels about the decision, Woodman, who used to coach in the Arsenal academy system, states: ‘Yeah, I feel betrayed. Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair. That’s fine, I get how the football business works.

    According to recent reports, ‘But the bit that didn't sit comfortably with me was the conversations I was having with people at the club or owners, everyone above me… there was no inkling of any of this. I feel misled. I was surprised.

    According to recent reports, ‘One day, we were talking about prepares and the way forward and how to get through this sticky little period with players out injured, then the next minute it was a change of direction. Nothing like, “Right, you’ve got three games to turn it round”, none of that, nothing.

    ‘My record was good there, the owner always said if anyone can churn out results it was myself. Football has no patience. In football, people always forget where they come from. I understand wanting to move forward. It’s disappointing really, that’s the best word I can use. I feel let down.

    ‘It was just a normal day when they told me. I was going into training, popped across to where the chairman’s office was and then was just told, “We are going to take a change of direction”. It was no more than that, I didn’t try to change the decision or ask why.

    ‘It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is… I am sure people will read this and think, “You deserve this” and “You deserve that” but what else can you do? There’s no easy way of doing it.

    It has been revealed that 'When you have been told you are sacked, you don’t really want to stick around and have a long conversation. They didn’t give an explanation. They needed results, they remarked. We lost to Leicester which was not a great result, obviously. But realistically they are Leicester… and we are Bromley.’.

    It has been revealed that 'It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is'.

    Woodman, who used to be the Arsenal youth team goalkeeping coach, says: 'When I left Bromley that day, I just felt in shock to be really honest'.

    To hammer home that last point: Woodman’s first game was against Wealdstone in April 2021 in the National League at Hayes Lane. On that same weekend, Leicester were hosting soon-to-be champions Manchester City. Oh, and the Foxes won the FA Cup a month later.

    ‘When I left that day, I just felt in shock to be honest,’ continues Woodman. ‘I felt the next three games were winnable. I had played seven of the top 10 teams, beaten the top team Huddersfield, my goalie was just coming back from injury and some others were coming back.

    ‘We had two teams in the bottom four and one just outside so I felt it was my best opportunity to get some much-needed results.

    It has been revealed that ‘To take someone out who has been in football 40 years and been in coaching 25 years and then to put (his former assistant) Byron Webster in charge who had just been fresh out of playing and has never done a coaching session… with every respect, it feels unfair to him. It was a stupid thing to do. I found that really strange, they took one point from those three games. It fascinates me.’.

    Industry observers note that now, with Bromley bottom of League One, Karl Robinson, the former Salford and MK Dons boss, has taken over. Woodman, though, is keen not to sound bitter and will remember his five-and-a-half years at the club with fondness. He claims his best memories are taking Bromley into the Football League, playing at Newcastle in the FA Cup and beating ‘Hollywood Netflix club Wrexham’ in the FA Trophy final.

    Sir Gareth Southgate remains his best friend, the pair having met as teenagers in the Crystal Palace academy. They took turns in being best man at each other’s wedding and Southgate is godfather of goalkeeper Andy’s son Freddie, who is on Liverpool’s books.

    They also co-authored the 2004 book Woody and Nord which chronicles two polar opposite career paths that started at the same level, one going on to play (and later manage) England, the other a journeyman in the lower leagues.

    ‘Nothing surprises Gareth and I,’ adds Woodman. ‘We have been in the game for 40 years now. You can argue that in his tenure at England, he got them as high as they have ever been in 60 years and it still was not enough. So it doesn’t surprise us. People have to make decisions and they are business-related, only time will tell if it is the right decision but that’s not my problem any more.

    Woodman and lifelong friend Sir Gareth Southgate at the release of their 2004 book 'Woody and Nord' which charts two very different careers in football.

    Southgate is godfather to Woodman's son Freddie, a goalkeeper on Liverpool's books.

    ‘Gareth was very supportive, so was Alan Pardew and the support from the Premier League right down to the National League, there has been no end of messages I have had, which is comforting.

    ‘That first Saturday after being out, I didn’t want to be watching or listening to the game, I just wanted to get away because that is the worst. I have had two clubs ring me, there are ongoing conversations and I am just making sure it is the right vehicle for me. What I mean by that is I want an owner that is aligned and who thinks they can compete to get out of their league.

    Recent findings suggest that ‘My record speaks for itself. If you ask most managers how many promotions and trophies they have won, I bet over long careers, they haven’t got many. For me, with the smallest budget in the leagues, we maximised the team and maximised success.

    Sources indicate that ‘To get two promotions and an FA Trophy win against Wrexham, hitting the play-offs four times in five years, that is something I am really proud of. If nothing else, the Bromley supporters and town are grateful.’.

    Industry observers note that fill in your charts, Scorigami fans: We have yet another score that had never happened before in 107 years of NFL history. The 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys is the first 46-40 game on record.

    It took some oddities and some late-game madness to get there, as is pretty much always the case when looking for a unique score. There were five touchdowns, a failed two-point conversion and two successful two-point conversions in the fourth quarter alone!

    Sources indicate that SF 46 - DAL 40🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨That is the 1099th unique score in NFL history, and the 4th of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/qW3tfAiLSJ.

    Recent findings suggest that entering the fourth quarter, the 49ers led 31-19, not a super common score, but nothing too absurd: That score has happened 17 times before. A missed Brandon Aubrey extra point earlier in the game created the strange number for Dallas.

    Recent findings suggest that then all hell (or, for Scorigami fans, heaven) broke loose. Christian McCaffrey scored on a 16-yard run. Dallas answered with a long touchdown drive but failed on the two-point conversion. At 38-25, the scoring chances rose. As a general rule, as the score rises astronomically, so, too, do the chances for a unique score. The Cowboys got a stop and scored again, this time kicking the extra point to make it 38-32. That score has happened before, albeit only three times.

    In a recent development, it took just two plays for the 49ers to find the end zone, with Brock Purdy finding McCaffrey jetting off for a 66-yard touchdown. Purdy also found McCaffrey for the two-point conversion. That was big, because 44-32 and 45-32 have both happened before (once each). But 46-32 had never happened before.

    Recent findings suggest that luckily, one final Dak Prescott touchdown pass and, crucially, a successful two-point conversion didn't ruin things, either. The two-point conversion was actually crucial, because 46-38 has happened before. So, everyone, please applaud Dak Prescott's effort here.

    Dak converts the two-point conversion!We've got a six-point game 👀SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SjVjt43GD9.

    The next Scorigami will be the 1,100th unique score in NFL history, and hopefully, it will be half as fun as this game was. This was also the fourth Scorigami this season, a rare feat in itself.

Texas could stand to upgrade at first base and could always slot Sato in at DH as well.

    We ranked Sato as the fourth-best free agent available and the best free agent position player. The reigning Triple Crown winner in Japan hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026.     It was a day of statement wins around the NFL and the biggest statement was made by the Minnesota Vikings.

    In their first game since trading for Kirk Cousins, the Vikings pounded the Packers 30-10, and the impressive part is that they did that at Lambeau Field. Combined with their 39-22 win in Week 1, they became the first team since 1987 to beat the Packers by at least 17 points twice in a season.

    Patrick Mahomes also made a statement on Sunday and that's the Chiefs offense can still function just fine without Kenneth Walker. In Kansas City's 35-13 win over Atlanta, Mahomes threw five TD passes in a game for the first time since 2022. He also threw for 348 yards, and a big reason was that he finally had the long ball working. Mahomes, who had gone 20 straight games without throwing a touchdown pass that traveled at least 20 yards in the air, produced two of those against the Falcons.

    Industry observers note that deshaun Watson also made a statement. The Browns quarterback led ANOTHER fourth-quarter comeback and just became only the third QB in NFL history with a game-winning drive in each of his team's first six wins in a season (1990 Troy Aikman and 2016 Matthew Stafford).

    And then there was Joe Burrow. The Bengals QB made a statement on Sunday night against the Steelers with four touchdown passes in a dominating 38-18 win. Burrow now has at least four total touchdowns in five straight games, which is tied with Peyton Manning (2004) for the longest streak in NFL history.

    And now, it's time for the Week 10 grades, and we're going to start with the Vikings, who are starting to look pretty super.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m.
    • Skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly.
    • Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Barring a surprise agreement, the owners are almost certain to lock out the players at that time. Skubal is expected to sign before then.

    Skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly. There's a real chance Skubal signs a contract worth more than $400 million in the next two weeks or so. Excluding Shohei Ohtani, who is technically a pitcher but is really a two-way player, here are the largest pitching contracts in history:.

    According to recent reports, 1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    It has been revealed that 3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    Industry observers note that 3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    According to recent reports, 4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    It has been revealed that something like, say, eight years at $50 million a year would give Skubal a $400 million contract that obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee and average annual value. Several big-market clubs are mentioned to be pursuing Skubal (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), who is a special free agent as an in-his-prime ace. Conditions are ripe for a record deal.

    There is also a chance Skubal goes the Valdez route, or the Bo Bichette/Kyle Tucker route, and signs a short-term contract with a high annual salary. It might only be a small chance, but there is a chance. The Athletic reports the Dodgers prefer such an arrangement with Skubal. ESPN indicates Skubal has no interest in such a deal, though minds can always be changed.

    According to recent reports, with that in mind, here are the pros and cons of a high-dollar, short-term contract for Skubal. Keep in mind that such a contract is usually a three- or four-year deal with opt outs, not a straight one- or two-year contract, and Skubal wouldn't necessarily have to use the opt outs to re-enter free agency. He could leverage them into a new contract to stay with his team.

    1. Maximize earnings. Plain and simple, a short-term contract would give Skubal a chance to max out his earnings by making free agency available to him again as soon as next offseason. Go out, have a typical Skubal season in 2027, and perhaps market forces push the demand even higher than it is right now. Remember that, along with a salary cap, there could be a salary floor in the future. Small-market contenders like, say, the Guardians or Rays could throw many millions at Skubal to reach the floor in the future.

    Sources indicate that 2. Chance to set more records. This ties back to the last point. Skubal already set a new salary record for an arbitration-eligible player ($32 million in 2026) and he's positioned to set a new standard for pitcher contracts this offseason. Go back into free agency in a year or two, and Skubal (and Boras) could have a chance to break his own pitcher contract record. The record itself won't be a driving factor in that decision (the money will ultimately decide things), but it would be a nice feather in his cap.

    Recent findings suggest that 3. Freedom to change teams. Sometimes things don't work out. I don't think Juan Soto expected to miss the postseason in the first two years of his record 15-year, $765 million contract with the Mets. It's entirely possible Skubal could find his next situation not to his liking for whatever reason. Maybe the team doesn't contend, maybe he clashes with the coaching staff, maybe he doesn't like the local breakfast taco options. There could be a million different reasons it doesn't work. A short-term, high-dollar deal would give Skubal an escape hatch and allow him to head elsewhere if things go sideways.

    Recent findings suggest that 1. Injury and performance risk. All things considered, Skubal is a pretty safe bet on a long-term contract, though he is a pitcher, and pitchers get hurt. It's what they do. Skubal has had three elbow surgeries, including Tommy John surgery in 2017 and a minor procedure this May. If he gets hurt again, or his performance slips for whatever reason, then he could wind up costing himself in the big picture because he won't be able to opt out and sign a larger deal. A short-term, high-dollar contract will pay him handsomely. He won't struggle to put bread on the table. But injury/performance risk means Skubal could ultimately leave money on the table.

    2. Potential salary cap. It is possible the next CBA will include a salary cap, which could limit Skubal's market and earning potential should he go back out into free agency in a year or two (or three). It's not just the cap itself either. MLB has proposed contract limits as part of the salary cap: five years at 15% of the cap for players who change teams, or six years at 16% of the cap for players who remain with their current team. Even if MLB doesn't get a salary cap and instead the competitive balance tax system remains in place with stiffer penalties, that could cost Skubal in the future. This offseason might be his last chance to sign in a truly free market.

    #3180. Naz Reid landing spots: Four NBA contenders that make sense if Hornets look to move sharp-shooting big man

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Naz Reid landing spots: Four NBA contenders that make sense if Hornets look to move sharp-shooting big man

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • You could argue that before this season, there was not a single role player in the NBA more beloved by his own fanbase than Naz Reid.
    • Recent findings suggest that reid, 27, is posting major raw numbers in his first season as a full-time starter with the Charlotte Hornets, but there are bigger concerns under the surface.
    • Recent findings suggest that reid, along with an unprotected 2033 first-round pick, was one of the centerpieces of Charlotte's return in trading star guard LaMelo Ball to Minnesota.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    You could argue that before this season, there was not a single role player in the NBA more beloved by his own fanbase than Naz Reid. Simply uttering his name, devoid of context, became a popular meme among the Minnesota Timberwolves faithful in recent years, and for good reason. The former undrafted free agent grew into a Sixth Man of the Year winner and one of the best shooting bigs in basketball during his seven-year run with the Timberwolves. Leaving the only team he had ever known this offseason has proven difficult thus far.

    Recent findings suggest that reid, 27, is posting major raw numbers in his first season as a full-time starter with the Charlotte Hornets, but there are bigger concerns under the surface. After shooting just under 57% on 2-pointers in Minnesota, he is at around 44% with the Hornets and struggling to score efficiently near the basket. His defense has raised eyebrows as well, and after he was benched in an early game against the Detroit Pistons, Hornets coach Charles Lee remarked that Reid "didn't meet our standards in the first half, and at halftime we made the decision that he wouldn't play in the second half.".

    Recent findings suggest that reid, along with an unprotected 2033 first-round pick, was one of the centerpieces of Charlotte's return in trading star guard LaMelo Ball to Minnesota. The 4-7 Hornets have struggled mightily without Ball, posting the NBA's worst offensive rating this season despite having the league's best offense from early December forward last season. Injuries have played a massive part in those struggles, but at this stage, Reid's role as a foundational Hornets player moving forward is already coming into question. Timberwolves beat writer Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic even stated on his podcast that the chances of Reid getting traded again are "very high.".

    Sources indicate that "The Hornets now are clearly in a period of transition, and they decided that LaMelo Ball was not going to be a part of the team that they believe can eventually get to real contender status," Krawczynski explained. "They made a decision with that core group that they were not good enough as constructed and so they had to take a step back, amass some assets and go forward. And what that also means is that, A, the fans are going to be upset because they finally had a fun season last year and now it is going sideways again, but B, the possibilities of Naz Reid getting traded again are very high. This is a roster that I think is going to change over quite a bit over the next couple of years as the Hornets look for the right combination of people to really vault into what they hope is contention.".

    Krawczynski did not specify a timetable, and we've certainly seen frustrating starts turn into fruitful long-term partnerships, but all of this underlines just how difficult things have been for Reid and the Hornets so far this season. Charlotte knew what it was doing by trading Ball. The idea was to take a step back now to take a bigger step forward later. If that's still the idea here, there should be plenty of teams with real interest in Reid, so let's identify a few possible landing spots for the sweet-shooting big man.

    According to recent reports, the Warriors traded for and eventually re-signed Kristaps Porziņģis because they need substantial men who can shoot in a lineup featuring both Draymond Green and, presumably, Jimmy Butler eventually. Al Horford can cover some of those minutes, but he's 40 and can only be expected to play so much. Fortunately, Green's ability to defend across the positional spectrum means the Warriors don't necessarily need their center-sized shooter to actually defend centers. If he's big, he rebounds and he shoots, he'll fit.

    This is Reid to a T. With Green on the team to actually guard the most dangerous centers and the combination of Butler and Yaxel Lendeborg providing size on the wing, the Warriors are fairly well-equipped to minimize Reid's weaknesses. His strengths are exactly what the Warriors need; the not-currently-getting-paid Porziņģis takes Golden State most of the way there when it comes to salary matching (with only a smaller salary like Gui Santos or De'Anthony Melton needed to close the hard cap gap), and the Warriors control almost all of their own future draft capital, so they have the ammunition they'd need to satisfy the Hornets.

    The big question here -- especially with Stephen Curry now set to miss around a month with an oblique abdominal tear -- is how eager the Warriors are to invest in their present. Before the season, the answer should have been a resounding "not at all." But Curry was playing like an MVP candidate before he got hurt, and the emergence of Lendeborg as the Rookie of the Year favorite has arguably changed the equation. While the Warriors (8-4) may not be able to justify an all-in trade, giving up, say, one unprotected pick to nab the 27-year-old Reid, who can be a part of their post-Curry future as well as their present, might be a satisfactory compromise.

    According to recent reports, the Pistons have reportedly had an eye on Reid ever since his anticipated 2025 free agency, but he wound up re-signing with Minnesota before the opening bell even rang. The appeal is obvious. Two of Detroit's three best players, Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren, are non-shooters. Having a big man who can shoot theoretically helps offset that deficit, particularly in lineups featuring just one of those two. Detroit tried that very strategy this offseason in acquiring John Collins. The results have been mixed, with the Pistons faring far better in the minutes Collins sits than the ones he plays. Reid is better and younger.

    The Pistons are enormously flexible in how they could construct a deal. They control all of their own first-round picks, and they have a fair bit of breathing room beneath the luxury tax. That breathing room evaporates next season, though, when Thompson's rookie extension kicks in. This is where the decision calculus gets harder. Duren and Cade Cunningham are already making market rate. Thompson will be next season, and Duncan Robinson has simply proven too indispensable to move on from. Paying all four of those players plus Reid would leave precious little flexibility to add the second ball-handler Detroit badly needs.

    Recent findings suggest that maybe the Pistons feel they're good enough as is to win without one, or they could be prepared to trade someone else out of their core down the line if they feel compelled to seek out that needed ball-handling addition. The Trajan Langdon-led front office is now in its third season at the helm, yet it has not traded a single first-round pick amid Detroit's ascent. The Pistons have been cautious with buy-now moves. Maybe Reid is the sort of player they'd splurge for, but considering how well the Pistons are playing, they will likely be cautious in shaking things up too much.

    According to recent reports, cleveland's starting five simply hasn't worked this season. The Cavaliers are getting crushed with their five starters on the floor, and the Jarrett Allen-Evan Mobley duo, a frequent target of the rumor mill, is losing its minutes together by over five points per 100 possessions. That duo has never generated the elite rebounding that double-significant lineups are supposed to create, and while they do a good job of defending shots at the rim, they give up so many of them that they net out as a fairly underwhelming rim defense. Peyton Watson is struggling to fit in as a small forward, but lineups featuring him and just one of Mobley or Allen are faring far better.

    In a recent development, swapping one of the bigs out for Reid, essentially trading defense for shooting, recalibrates the team in ways that theoretically create a friendlier environment for Watson. The Hornets, still presumably looking for a long-term starter at center, would likely have some degree of interest in either Mobley or Allen. The question is which makes more sense in a trade like this.

    The answer is probably Allen. He's older. He's worse. He's more traditionally a center than Mobley, whom Cleveland has historically been reluctant to move up from power forward. But the on-off data is pretty clear this season: Cleveland is playing better with Allen on the floor than it is with Mobley. If the Cavaliers are going to go with a single major, it might behoove them to stick with the one they know can be a center. Mobley's 30% max contract is going to prove limiting down the line, especially with Donovan Mitchell starting a 35% supermax deal next season. Mobley would almost certainly net more in a trade than Allen would, and Charlotte has the pick surplus to make a pretty compelling offer if it wants to.

    If Mobley is available in any way, shape or form by February, offers will come in from several teams. Not many have a package that makes more immediate sense than one built around Reid and Charlotte's picks, which Cleveland could either keep or redirect for other assets. If Cleveland and Charlotte do engage on Reid talks, though, Allen is the far likelier Cavaliers big man to become a Hornet.

    We can't fully judge the Raptors until we see an extended stretch with a healthy Kawhi Leonard, but thus far, Toronto's shooting weakness elsewhere has been as severe as expected. The Raptors rank 24th in 3-point attempt rate and 27th in 3-point percentage as of this writing. Like Golden State, Toronto is perfectly equipped to cover for Reid's deficiencies as a rim protector. There isn't a better trio of defensive forwards in the NBA than Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles, and Murray-Boyles already plays a reasonable amount of center.

    The money would presumably be RJ Barrett's expiring contract. Losing his shot-creation would sting, but with a healthy Leonard, they should be covered in that respect. The question is draft compensation. The Raptors already gave up unprotected picks in 2031 and 2033 for Leonard, leaving their 2029 selection as their only tradable, unencumbered pick. They could move their 2027 pick as well, though it has swap rights attached to the Oklahoma City Thunder, limiting its appeal. A swap or two would probably be needed here to seal the deal, but Toronto probably has the chips to pull this off if it's motivated enough.

    Reid would eat up Toronto's room beneath the luxury tax line next season, but with all of their core players locked in, that shouldn't be much of an issue. The Raptors haven't started their tax clock yet, so a year or two above that line (and still well below the dreaded second apron) seems a small price to pay for a genuine championship contender.

    Cover 32: Two NFL awards already in the bag, plus game balls, biggest gaffes from Week 10
